summary: Crow's nest on a butte north-northeast of Coeur d'Alene, abandoned in 1947; today a popular trail area with communication towers on the ridge.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1947. No source we read describes a lookout structure on the site today.

access.note: A hiker's account describes a very accessible, very popular trail system and gives driving directions to the trailhead, but it does not say who may enter. We found no agency statement on access. The account also says the route leaves city land for an LLC-labelled area.

visit.trail_note: About 1.8 miles one way to the summit from the Canfield Mountain Nature Trail West parking area, per a hiker's account.

notes_for_editor: Four pages agree on the 1932 crow's nest, the west-butte patrol point and the 1947 abandonment. Today's account rests on one undated personal hiking page (WillhiteWeb), which is the only source for the trails and the towers; no agency statement on access was found. The same page says the route crosses city land and an LLC-labelled area, so check land status before any visit advice. The Idaho FFLA state list (firelookout.org/lookouts/us/id) has no Canfield Butte entry. The record's 47.7314, -116.73172 point was not checked against a map. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page says no staffing history is documented, so no staffing facts are given. In the verification pass the access level was set back to 'unknown' from 'public': the hiker's account gives driving directions and calls the trails popular, but does not say who may enter, and no agency statement was found. The first sentence of the story now carries footnote 1, and two sentences were reworded so they no longer copy a source's wording. The editor should check land status before any visit advice.
